```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Isolate package loading from storage initialization in this implementation guide.
(function() {
  previous <- Sys.getenv("TARR_POP_SKIP_CUBE_SETUP", unset = NA_character_)
  on.exit({
    if (is.na(previous)) Sys.unsetenv("TARR_POP_SKIP_CUBE_SETUP") else
      Sys.setenv(TARR_POP_SKIP_CUBE_SETUP = previous)
  })
  Sys.setenv(TARR_POP_SKIP_CUBE_SETUP = "true")
  library(tarr.pop)
})()
```

## What this guide explains

`open_poparray()` locates an HDF5 file, reconstructs the meaning of its axes from
stored metadata, and returns a delayed `poparray`. It connects storage lookup,
metadata decoding, the HDF5Array backend, and the package's object contract.
Understanding those connections helps explain why opening a cube usually needs
little population-data memory, why an unregistered file can still be opened, and
why malformed metadata can prevent opening an otherwise readable HDF5 file.

This is a source-level walkthrough of the implementation reviewed at development
version **0.0.0.9223**, based on commit **eaadf44**. The diagrams show package-level
calls and decisions. Repeated per-dimension loops and library-internal calls are
condensed; arrows do not imply that independent-looking readers run in parallel.
The text distinguishes the actual execution order from supporting data flow.

The main implementation is in
[R/open_pop_array.r](https://github.com/RussJones007/tarr.pop/blob/eaadf44/R/open_pop_array.r).
Storage configuration is in
[R/cube_storage.R](https://github.com/RussJones007/tarr.pop/blob/eaadf44/R/cube_storage.R),
object construction in
[R/poparray_class.r](https://github.com/RussJones007/tarr.pop/blob/eaadf44/R/poparray_class.r),
and semantic/applicability validation in
[R/dim_semantics.r](https://github.com/RussJones007/tarr.pop/blob/eaadf44/R/dim_semantics.r)
and
[R/dim_applicability.R](https://github.com/RussJones007/tarr.pop/blob/eaadf44/R/dim_applicability.R).
These pinned sources make the walkthrough reproducible when the package later changes.

Support functions discussed below are mostly internal. Calls using `tarr.pop:::`
in the tracing example deliberately inspect those internals; they are not a
recommended replacement for the public opening API.

The examples require a package installation containing the current `filepath`
entry point. Updating a Git checkout does not update the installed R package.
Check `packageVersion("tarr.pop")` and `args(tarr.pop::open_poparray)` if an
example reports an unused `filepath` argument. During repository development,
`devtools::load_all()` loads the working source; otherwise install the current
package and check `.libPaths()` for an older installation taking precedence.

### Opening versus package startup

The call sequence begins **after the package has loaded**. Package loading has its
own `.onLoad()` hook, which calls `tarr_pop_startup_setup()` and may initialize
configured storage through `init_cubes()`. Those startup actions are separate
from `open_poparray(filepath = ...)`. The setup chunk temporarily suppresses that
startup work so this guide uses only the bundled file and explicitly created
scratch directories. This distinction matters when interpreting a process-wide
trace: a registry scan during package startup is not evidence that direct-file
opening itself consulted the registry.

## The public entry point

The current signature is:

```r
open_poparray(series_id = NULL,
              dataset = "cube/population",
              data_col = NULL,
              checkout = FALSE,
              checkout_dir = tempdir(),
              filepath = NULL)
```

| Argument | What it controls |
|---|---|
| `series_id` | A logical series name looked up in configured storage. |
| `filepath` | A known HDF5 file, opened directly without registry lookup. |
| `dataset` | The numeric array within that file, normally `cube/population`. |
| `data_col` | An optional value-column name for the returned object and tabular output. |
| `checkout` | Whether to copy the entire backing file before opening it. |
| `checkout_dir` | The copy destination when checkout is requested. |

Exactly one of `series_id` and `filepath` must be supplied. Supplying neither or
both fails before storage lookup. `checkout` must be a non-missing logical scalar;
its directory argument is checked when checkout is enabled.

The compatibility function `open_tarr_pop(...)` simply forwards its arguments to
`open_poparray(...)`; it does not introduce another storage or metadata strategy.

```{r direct_example}
example_path <- system.file("extdata", "tdc_example.h5", package = "tarr.pop")
pop <- open_poparray(filepath = example_path)
list(class = class(pop)[1], dimensions = names(dimnames(pop)),
     time = time_role(pop), area = area_role(pop), value = data_col(pop))
```

## The complete opening sequence

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A["open_poparray(): validate arguments"] --> B{"Which input was supplied?"}
  B -->|filepath| C["Check file and normalize its path"]
  B -->|series_id| D["Resolve root, read registry, select row, resolve file"]
  C --> E{"checkout = TRUE?"}
  D --> E
  E -->|yes| F["checkout_poparray(): copy file; keep original path"]
  E -->|no| G["get_cube_metadata_cached(path)"]
  F --> G
  G --> H["HDF5Array::HDF5Array(): create delayed dataset handle"]
  H --> I["Read cached labels, roles, semantics, source, value name"]
  I --> J["validate_labels_against_cube(): compare extents"]
  J --> K["Attach dimnames to the handle"]
  K --> L["new_poparray(): validate and construct S4 object"]
  L --> M["If checked out, attach backing_file attribute"]
  M --> N["Return delayed poparray"]
```

Once a file has been resolved, both entry paths use the same sequence. The
metadata bundle is obtained **before** the delayed HDF5 dataset handle is created.
On a cold cache, this bundle already includes parsed semantic objects. The later
reader functions usually extract those prepared fields rather than reconstruct
semantics a second time.

| Order after locating the file | Actual function or operation | Result passed onward |
|---|---|---|
| 1, optional | `checkout_poparray()` | A copy's normalized path; original path retained separately. |
| 2 | `get_cube_metadata_cached()` | One bundle named `meta`. |
| 3 | `HDF5Array::HDF5Array()` | The delayed dataset handle named `h5`. |
| 4 | `read_dimnames_from_cube()` | Named coordinate vectors named `dimn`. |
| 5 | `read_roles_from_cube()` | Time, area, and stored strata roles. |
| 6 | `read_dim_semantics_from_cube()` | Named per-axis semantic objects. |
| 7 | `read_source_from_cube()` | Provenance fields. |
| 8, conditional | `read_data_col_from_cube()` | Stored value-column name, unless overridden. |
| 9 | `validate_labels_against_cube()` | Confirmation that handle extents match label lengths. |
| 10 | `dimnames(h5) <- dimn` | Labels attached to the in-memory delayed handle. |
| 11 | `new_poparray()` | The role-aware S4 `poparray`. |
| 12, optional | `attr(pa, "backing_file") <- backing_file` | A reference to the original file when checkout was used. |

Attaching names to `h5` changes the R handle. It does not rewrite the HDF5 dataset
or its stored metadata. The opening function also does not rebuild the registry,
repair interrupted metadata edits, migrate a file, or save the returned object.

## Path A: opening a known file

The direct-file path uses `checkmate::assert_string()` and
`checkmate::assert_file_exists()`, then `normalizePath(..., mustWork = TRUE)`.
The normalized file path also becomes the label used in dimension-mismatch
messages. There is no call to `resolve_cube_dir()`, `tarr_series_registry()`, or
`resolve_registry_filepath()` in this branch.

This is useful for portable examples, tests, and scripts whose input file is
already known. The bundled cube does not need a matching registry row for the
example above to succeed. A valid file still needs the metadata layout and
semantic contract expected by the remainder of the opener.

## Path B: resolving a registered series

A series name first needs a storage root, then a registry row, then a physical
file. The registry is a lightweight locator; the selected HDF5 file remains the
source of dimensional and semantic metadata.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A["resolve_cube_dir()"] --> B["cube_path(create = FALSE)"]
  B --> C["configured_cube_path(): option, then YAML config"]
  C --> D{"Configured path available?"}
  D -->|yes| E["Verify root directory and normalize path"]
  D -->|no| F["Interactive prompt or configuration error"]
  F -->|path chosen| E
  E --> G["tarr_series_registry(root)"]
  G --> H{"Memoised registry available?"}
  H -->|yes| L["Return registry data frame"]
  H -->|no| I[".tarr_series_registry_impl()"]
  I --> J["cube_registry_cache_file() then read_cube_registry_cache()"]
  J --> K["Check required columns and unique, nonblank series IDs"]
  K --> L
  L --> M["open_poparray(): select exactly one series row"]
  M --> N["resolve_registry_filepath(): stored path, then filename fallback"]
  N --> O["Normalize first existing candidate"]
```

### Resolving the storage root

`resolve_cube_dir()` calls `cube_path(create = FALSE)` and verifies that the
resulting directory exists. Its `legacy_ok` argument is forwarded for
compatibility, but the current `cube_path()` ignores that deprecated argument;
it does not automatically fall back to package `extdata`.

`cube_path()` calls `configured_cube_path()`. That helper first checks the
`tarr.pop.cube_path` R option. If it is absent, `read_cube_path_config()` reads the
user's YAML configuration. `tarr_pop_config_file()` builds that configuration
filename using `tarr_pop_config_dir()`, which delegates to `tools::R_user_dir()`.

Without configuration, `prompt_for_cube_path()` offers an interactive prompt.
Its default comes from `tarr_pop_default_cube_path()` and
`tarr_pop_data_dir()`. A selected path is handled by `set_cube_path()`, which can
call `write_cube_path_config()` to persist the choice. In a non-interactive
session, the prompt returns no choice and the required-root lookup fails with a
configuration error. This first-use configuration case can write a YAML file;
it should not be confused with rewriting cube metadata or population values.

### Reading the registry

`tarr_series_registry()` normalizes the root and calls
`.tarr_series_registry_memoised()`. Memoise holds a registry result in process
memory. On a cache miss, `.tarr_series_registry_impl()` locates
`cache/cube_registry.rds` through `cube_registry_cache_file()` and its storage-path
helpers, then calls `read_cube_registry_cache()`.

`read_cube_registry_cache()` reads an RDS data frame. It requires `series_id`,
`filepath`, and `filename` columns and normalizes them to character vectors. A
missing, unreadable, or structurally unsuitable cache returns `NULL`; the caller
then reports that the registry must be initialized or rebuilt.
`.tarr_series_registry_impl()` additionally rejects missing, blank, and duplicate
series IDs. The opener selects the requested ID and requires exactly one row.
Its duplicate-row check is an additional defensive check after the registry's
own uniqueness validation.

### Finding the file named by a row

`resolve_registry_filepath()` tries the row's stored `filepath` first. It also
builds a candidate from `filename` and `resolve_cube_base_dir(root)`. That helper
uses `base/` when it exists, otherwise the root itself. The first existing
candidate is normalized and returned. If none exists, the error points the user
toward rebuilding the registry after moving, removing, or replacing files.

This fallback helps when a recorded absolute path is obsolete but the filename
still identifies a cube in the active base directory. It is not a recursive
search for similarly named files, and a registry row is not proof that a file's
complete semantic metadata is valid.

### Registry construction is separate from lookup

`rebuild_poparray_registry()` is an explicit preparation operation. It calls
`cube_registry_inventory()` to enumerate HDF5 files, `build_poparray_registry()`
to screen their layouts and build rows, and `write_cube_registry_cache()` to save
the index. `build_poparray_registry()` uses `h5_inventory()`,
`h5_has_cube_schema()`, and `read_series_row()`. The latter reads identifying
metadata, with compatibility fallbacks for series names and optional registry
fields. `read_registry_row()` is an older alias for that row reader.

These helpers do not run automatically when `open_poparray()` sees an unknown
series. Rebuilding invalidates the memoised registry and inventory results.
`init_cubes()` is a higher-level setup operation that prepares directories,
may copy bundled files, and rebuilds the registry.

```{r registered_example}
registered_example <- (function() {
  root <- tempfile("opening-guide-registry-")
  previous <- getOption("tarr.pop.cube_path")
  on.exit({
    options(tarr.pop.cube_path = previous)
    unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
  }, add = TRUE)
  set_cube_path(root, persist = FALSE)
  dir.create(file.path(root, "base"))
  stopifnot(file.copy(example_path,
                     file.path(root, "base", basename(example_path))))
  # This preparation is explicit, not an implicit step inside open_poparray().
  registry <- rebuild_poparray_registry(root)
  series <- registry$series_id[[1L]]
  registered <- open_poparray(series_id = series)
  stopifnot(identical(dimnames(registered), dimnames(pop)))
  list(series_id = series, registry_columns = names(registry),
       dimensions = names(dimnames(registered)))
})()
registered_example
```

The example restores the previous storage option and removes only its temporary
root. It does not persist a new user configuration or modify a production cube.

## Optional checkout: copying the backing file

`checkout_poparray()` checks the source and destination arguments, verifies the
source exists, creates the destination directory when needed, and calls
`file.copy()` with overwrite enabled and file mode/date preservation. The
filename is the source's basename. It returns the normalized destination path.

The opener keeps the original path in `backing_file`, switches its active path to
the copy, and subsequently reads metadata and creates the HDF5Array handle from
that copy. After construction it attaches the original path as the
`backing_file` attribute. Source/provenance metadata comes from the copied file;
checkout does not invent a new provenance record or automatically save analysis
changes back to the source.

Copying remains different from realizing an array in R: the entire file,
including population bytes and other HDF5 content, is copied through the
filesystem. This can be substantial I/O even though population values are not
expanded into an ordinary R array. A unique checkout directory avoids basename
collisions and accidental overwriting of an earlier copy.

```{r checkout_example}
checkout_details <- (function() {
  destination <- tempfile("opening-guide-checkout-")
  on.exit(unlink(destination, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  copied <- open_poparray(filepath = example_path, checkout = TRUE,
                         checkout_dir = destination)
  seed_path <- DelayedArray::seed(copied)@filepath
  stopifnot(file.exists(seed_path),
            identical(dimnames(copied), dimnames(pop)))
  list(copy_exists = file.exists(seed_path),
       copy_uses_requested_directory = identical(dirname(seed_path),
                                                 normalizePath(destination)),
       original_file = basename(attr(copied, "backing_file")))
})()
checkout_details
```

## Loading and caching the metadata bundle

The process-memory environment `.cube_metadata_cache` stores metadata bundles.
It is distinct from the memoised registry and from the RDS registry file on disk.
No population array is stored in this metadata cache.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A["get_cube_metadata_cached(path, refresh = FALSE)"] --> B["cube_metadata_path_cache_key(path)"]
  B --> C{"Not refreshing and path key exists?"}
  C -->|yes| D["Return cached bundle immediately"]
  C -->|no| E["cube_metadata_cache_key(): normalized path and file mtime"]
  E --> F{"Timestamp key exists?"}
  F -->|yes| G["assign_cube_metadata_cache(): add aliases"]
  G --> D
  F -->|no| H["get_cube_metadata()"]
  H --> I["h5_inventory() and metadata h5read calls"]
  I --> J["parse_dim_semantics_from_meta()"]
  J --> K["assign_cube_metadata_cache(): store bundle under keys"]
  K --> D
```

### The cache helpers and their limits

`cube_metadata_path_cache_key()` makes a key from the supplied path string.
`cube_metadata_cache_key()` verifies the file exists and combines its normalized
path with a formatted modification time. `assign_cube_metadata_cache()` puts the
bundle into the environment under the requested keys and a path alias.

An ordinary path-key hit returns immediately, **without checking modification
time**. Therefore normal opening is not an automatic out-of-process file-change
detector. The internal `refresh = TRUE` flag bypasses that first lookup, but can
still reuse a timestamp-key entry; it is not an unconditional disk reread.
Same-key external edits or timestamp preservation can therefore matter.

`reset_poparray_cache()` clears the metadata environment and forgets the memoised
registry and inventory results. It is an internal maintenance/testing helper,
used below to make a cold-start trace reproducible. A fresh R session also starts
with fresh process caches. Package writers and administration functions have
cache-management responsibilities of their own; external HDF5 edits should not
be assumed to refresh existing R objects or process caches automatically.

### Building a cold metadata bundle

`get_cube_metadata()` calls `h5_inventory()` unless an inventory was supplied.
The opener does not supply one. `h5_inventory()` uses `rhdf5::h5ls()` and disables
its `datasetinfo` option when that argument is available. This lists the HDF5
hierarchy; it does not extract the population dataset.

The inventory helpers `cube_info_has_entry()`, `h5_dataset_exists()`, and
`h5_group_exists()` check names, groups, and object types in the already available
inventory. They do not individually rescan the file. `h5_read_scalar_chr()` reads
one metadata value and converts its first element to character.
`h5_read_scalar_chr_if_present()` checks the inventory before reading an optional
scalar. With no supplied inventory it would perform its own inventory call, but
the cold bundle passes the shared inventory through.

| Bundle field | How `get_cube_metadata()` obtains it |
|---|---|
| `path` | Normalized file path. |
| `info` | Shared HDF5 hierarchy inventory. |
| `dim_order` | `cube/metadata/dim_order`, read with `rhdf5::h5read()`. |
| `dimnames` | One character vector under `cube/metadata/dimnames/<dimension>` per axis. |
| `roles` | Time and area scalars, plus stored strata labels. |
| `source` | Note, source, updated timestamp, and population type. |
| `data_col` | Optional stored name; absent or empty storage falls back to `"population"`. |
| `dim_semantics` | Parsed semantic objects described in the next section. |

The inventory can list history groups, but this bundle is not a full history
object. Opening does not call `cube_history()` or `cube_metadata_at()` to restore
a historical revision. It opens the current metadata and current population
dataset.

## Reconstructing semantic objects and applicability

`parse_dim_semantics_from_meta()` requires the
`cube/metadata/dim_semantics` group. For each dimension it checks whether the
complete current field layout is available. When it is, the parser calls
`read_dim_semantics_entry()` and constructs an S7 `DimSemantics` object through
`new_dim_semantics()`.

`read_dim_semantics_entry()` reads the dimension name, domain, scale type,
partition type, validation flag, overlap labels, notes, and optional
applicability. Its local `read_if_present()` closure handles optional scalar
fields using the shared inventory.

`read_dim_applicability()` looks for the nested applicability group. Absence
produces `NULL`. When present, it reads `by`, checks that `n_schemas` is a finite,
non-negative whole-number count, and reads each schema's `from`, `through`, and
`levels`. Its local `read_boundary()` closure turns a stored zero-length boundary
into `NULL`; a null boundary is later interpreted as an open endpoint in the
current controlling labels.

| Helper | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `parse_dim_semantics_from_meta()` | Select current or supported legacy layout; produce one named semantic object per axis. |
| `read_dim_semantics_entry()` | Read the fields for a current-layout semantic entry. |
| `read_dim_applicability()` | Restore the optional controller/schema list and validate the schema count. |
| `new_dim_semantics()` | Call the S7 `DimSemantics` constructor with decoded properties. |
| `pa_default_dim_domain()` | Supply a domain when translating supported legacy fields: time, area, age, or the dimension name. |
| `pa_default_dim_scale_type()` | Supply a legacy scale default: interval for time/`age.char`, nominal otherwise. |
| `pa_applicability_structure_problems()` | Describe malformed controller/schema structures during semantic validation. |

If a complete current layout is not found, the parser expects the supported
legacy `class` and `validated` fields. It translates `partition`, `set`, or an
unrecognized legacy class to the corresponding partition type/default. This is
an in-memory compatibility translation, not an on-disk migration. Missing
required legacy fields or a missing semantic group causes an error.

Applicability says which target categories are reported for each controller
period. It is restored as metadata, not applied by reading and rewriting values
during opening. Subsequent filtering and guarded reductions use it to distinguish
structural exclusions from applicable missing population counts.

## Creating the delayed handle and extracting cached fields

`HDF5Array::HDF5Array(filepath = path, name = dataset)` constructs the delayed
handle for the requested dataset. The backend inspects dataset metadata such as
shape and type; creating the handle is not `as.array()` and does not load the full
population cube into R.

The five package readers are deliberately small when called with `meta`:

| Reader | Field returned during normal opening |
|---|---|
| `read_dimnames_from_cube(path, meta)` | `meta$dimnames`. |
| `read_roles_from_cube(path, meta)` | `meta$roles`. |
| `read_dim_semantics_from_cube(..., meta)` | `meta$dim_semantics`, already parsed. |
| `read_source_from_cube(path, meta)` | `meta$source`. |
| `read_data_col_from_cube(path, meta)` | `meta$data_col`. |

The ordinary readers call `get_cube_metadata_cached()` themselves if `meta` was
not supplied. The semantic reader has a separate uncached fallback that builds a
minimal metadata context and calls the parser. Neither fallback is needed for
these readers in the normal opener, which passes its bundle explicitly.

With a `data_col` override, the opener skips `read_data_col_from_cube()` and uses
the requested name for the returned object. A cold metadata bundle still reads
the stored name while being assembled. The override changes neither the
population values nor the stored file metadata.

```{r value_name_override}
renamed_value <- open_poparray(filepath = example_path, data_col = "count")
c(object_name = data_col(renamed_value), stored_default = data_col(pop))
```

A custom `dataset` must have the extents and axis ordering expected by the cube's
metadata. The extent check cannot prove that another same-shaped dataset has the
same scientific meaning. The current object contract still requires the roles
and semantics of a population cube.

## Shape checks and S4 construction

`validate_labels_against_cube()` compares `dim(h5)` with the number of label
vectors and each vector's length. It raises a dimension-count or dimension-length
error before labels are attached to the handle. This is the explicit connection
between the physical dataset shape and the coordinate metadata.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A["new_poparray(h5, labels, roles, semantics, source, value name)"] --> B["Reject NULL semantics"]
  B --> C[".new_poparray_internal()"]
  C --> D["Check DelayedArray and HDF5-backed seed"]
  D --> E["Check named labels, value name, and distinct role names"]
  E --> F["validate_dim_semantics()"]
  F --> G["pa_validate_applicability() where applicable"]
  G --> H["methods::new: populate the S4 poparray"]
  H --> I["Populate compatibility attributes"]
  I --> J["Return object with delayed seed and metadata slots"]
```

`new_poparray()` is the public constructor. It rejects null semantics and delegates
to `.new_poparray_internal()` with strict semantic validation enabled. The
internal helper checks for a `DelayedArray`, an HDF5-backed seed, a named list of
labels, a single non-missing character value name, and distinct time/area names
present in that list.

`is_hdf5_backed_delayed()` checks the seed graph, including multi-seed delayed
operations. It inspects seed structures rather than extracting population values.
`validate_dim_semantics()` checks that semantic names match the axes in order,
that entries are S7 `DimSemantics` objects with consistent `dim_name` properties,
and that required role axes are declared partitions. It then checks
applicability against the current labels.

`pa_validate_applicability()` uses `pa_dim_applicability()` to retrieve optional
schemas, then `pa_applicability_indices()` to resolve their boundaries and levels.
The latter rejects self/missing controllers, unknown target levels, unknown or
reversed boundaries, overlapping schema ranges, and uncovered controller labels.
For interval partitions with active applicability schemas, semantic validation
also uses `pa_is_partition()`, `pa_is_interval()`, and
`pa_has_interval_overlap()` to reject overlapping or unrecognized interval
contributors. These checks inspect categories and schemas, not numeric counts.

`methods::new()` populates the S4 object slots. The constructor's explicit
semantic checks above are part of the opening sequence. Separately,
`methods::validObject(pop)` invokes registered S4 validity checks, including
inherited delayed-array validity. The `poparray` validity callback checks role
references, semantic names/types, applicability, grouping names, and metadata
shape consistency. These validity checks should be distinguished from the
selected calls observed during opening in the trace below.
`validate_hdf5_metadata_shape()` is an optional extra audit controlled by
`tarr.pop.audit_hdf5_metadata`, disabled by default. When enabled during validity
checking, it compares the object with cached HDF5 metadata where its
seed/dataset supports that audit.

The more general `validate_poparray()` also checks chronological ordering of time
labels when invoked by later operations such as `filter()`. It is not called
explicitly by the `open_poparray()` body. Opening should not be described as a
scan of all numeric data or a complete scientific audit: it does not validate
population counts by reading them, harmonize reporting schemas, or certify that
all axes can safely be summed.

### What the returned object contains

| Slot or component | Source |
|---|---|
| Delayed seed | The HDF5Array handle for the selected file and dataset. |
| `time_role`, `area_role` | Stored role names. |
| `strata_roles` | Recomputed as axes other than time and area. |
| `dim_semantics` | The decoded named semantic list. |
| `data_col` | Stored/default name or the caller's override. |
| `source` | Provenance converted to a list. |
| `dn_cache` | The named coordinate list for fast in-memory inspection. |
| `group_vars` | Empty by default; opening does not restore analysis grouping. |

The constructor also fills transitional `data_col`, `source`, and `dimroles`
attributes for compatibility. These attributes are secondary to the explicit
S4 slots. The stored strata field is read into the metadata bundle, but the
constructor derives the returned strata roles from the actual axis names and
required roles.

## Observing the call sequence in a running R session

The following maintainer-oriented example traces selected package functions for
one cold opening and one warm opening of the same bundled file. It logs function
**entries**, not execution times or every third-party call. Traces are removed on
exit, even if the example fails. Clearing process caches here is intentional and
should not be copied into every ordinary analysis script.

```{r observed_calls}
#| message: false
observed <- (function() {
  ns <- asNamespace("tarr.pop")
  functions <- c("open_poparray", "get_cube_metadata_cached", "get_cube_metadata",
    "h5_inventory", "parse_dim_semantics_from_meta", "read_dimnames_from_cube",
    "read_roles_from_cube", "read_dim_semantics_from_cube", "read_source_from_cube",
    "read_data_col_from_cube", "validate_labels_against_cube", "new_poparray",
    ".new_poparray_internal", "validate_dim_semantics", "pa_validate_applicability")
  audit <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  audit$events <- character()
  traced <- character()
  on.exit({
    for (name in traced) {
      invisible(capture.output(untrace(name, where = ns)))
    }
  }, add = TRUE)
  recorder <- function(name) {
    force(name)
    function() audit$events <- c(audit$events, name)
  }
  for (name in functions) {
    invisible(capture.output(trace(name, tracer = recorder(name),
                                   where = ns, print = FALSE)))
    traced <- c(traced, name)
  }
  tarr.pop:::reset_poparray_cache()
  cold <- tarr.pop::open_poparray(filepath = example_path)
  first <- audit$events
  audit$events <- character()
  warm <- tarr.pop::open_poparray(filepath = example_path)
  second <- audit$events
  stopifnot(identical(dimnames(cold), dimnames(warm)))
  list(
    inventory = data.frame(opening = c("cold", "warm"),
      package_inventory_calls = c(sum(first == "h5_inventory"),
                                  sum(second == "h5_inventory"))),
    calls = data.frame(opening = c(rep("cold", length(first)), rep("warm", length(second))),
      step = c(seq_along(first), seq_along(second)),
      function_name = c(first, second))
  )
})()
observed$inventory
observed$calls
```

A cold opening normally calls the package inventory once, while a warm path hit
avoids `get_cube_metadata()` and that inventory call. The warm opening still
creates a handle, checks shape, and constructs a new object. These counts concern
`h5_inventory()` specifically; HDF5Array can perform its own dataset-header I/O,
so they are not a count of all HDF5 library operations.

## Where population values are actually retrieved

Metadata reads are real I/O: coordinates, roles, semantics, and provenance must
be obtained when they are not cached. HDF5Array also needs structural information
about the selected dataset. Those operations do not materialize the full numeric
population cube. DelayedArray validity may perform zero-length extraction for
seed checking; that is not a full population-value scan.

A later `filter()` or named subset usually records a new delayed view. A
conversion or numerical reduction is a separate boundary. For example,
`as.array()` is **EAGER** for the current view, whereas a guarded cube sum or
`summarise()` reads values through the appropriate backend/reduction machinery.
Checkout is its own boundary: it copies file bytes even though array realization
is still delayed.

```{r realization_boundary}
# Select a single reported cell using named coordinates before retrieval.
one_cell <- pop[year = "2018", area.name = "Tarrant", sex = "female",
                age.char = "10", race.eth = "white", drop = FALSE]
dim(one_cell)
# EAGER, but only this selected R result is materialized.
as.array(one_cell)
```

An HDF5 chunk can contain more cells than the selected result, so physical reads
and decompression need not equal exactly one cell's bytes. The important memory
property is that this example does not expand the entire cube into an R array or
long table. A base R `rhdf5::h5read(path, "cube/population")` would instead be an
**EAGER** read of that dataset. Likewise, `as.data.frame(pop)` or
`tibble::as_tibble(pop)` expands the current cube view into a table; opening a
cube alone does neither.

## Diagnosing failures by stage

| Symptom | Stage to inspect | Explanation or next step |
|---|---|---|
| Exactly-one-input error | Argument validation | Choose either `series_id` or `filepath`. |
| Cube folder is not configured | Registered-series root resolution | Configure storage, or use an explicit file path. |
| No registry found | Registry RDS lookup | Prepare storage with `init_cubes()` or explicitly rebuild its registry. |
| Unknown/duplicate series | Registry validation and row selection | Inspect series IDs and rebuild after changing stored cubes. |
| Registered file not found | Candidate path resolution | Check stored paths and the base-directory filename fallback. |
| Checkout failure | Directory creation or file copy | Check source, destination, and copying permissions; use a unique directory. |
| Missing semantic group or fields | Metadata reconstruction | The file does not have a supported opening layout; migrate explicitly. |
| Dimension count/length mismatch | Handle-to-label shape validation | Dataset extents disagree with the stored coordinate list. |
| Role/semantic/applicability error | Constructor validation | Fix the inconsistent metadata contract rather than coercing away the class. |
| Old metadata after an external file edit | Process caches/existing handles | Do not assume a path hit refreshes itself; use a fresh session or deliberate internal cache maintenance. |

For interrupted metadata replacement, the appropriate administration workflow
may involve `recover_cube_metadata()` before reopening. Opening itself does not
perform that recovery. For scientific aggregation errors, inspect `overlaps()`
and applicability; successful opening is not permission to bypass those guards.

## Keeping this walkthrough current

When the opener changes, review the input branches, checkout placement, metadata
cache behavior, reader order, constructor arguments, and object validity checks.
Then execute the direct-file, temporary-registry, checkout, and trace examples.
The existing `test-open_pop_array.R` regression tests cover direct-path bypass,
registry failures, selected-cube inventories, dimensionality-independent hierarchy
scans, metadata consistency, checkout, and delayed backing. Related applicability
and class tests exercise the semantic/object contracts.

The call graph should describe actual conditional execution, not merely list
names found in a function body. In particular, preserve the distinctions between
explicit registry rebuilding and lookup, cache construction and cache reuse,
metadata inspection and population retrieval, and file copying and R realization.
